---
title: "GRCh38 Native Chromosome Learning Curves"
subtitle: "`r params$analysis_name` | `r params$negative_kind` negative backgrounds"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    number_sections: true
    theme: cosmo
params:
  alphagenome_metrics_path: null
  lsgkm_metrics_path: null
  analysis_name: null
  positive_class: null
  negative_kind: null
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE,
                      fig.width=10, fig.height=7, dpi=120)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(gt); library(scales)})
source("reports/chromosome_learning_helpers.R")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size=11) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor=element_blank(), legend.position="bottom"))
model_colors <- c(AlphaGenome="#0072B2", `LS-GKM`="#D55E00")
```

```{r inputs, include=FALSE}
required_params <- c("alphagenome_metrics_path", "lsgkm_metrics_path",
                     "analysis_name", "positive_class", "negative_kind")
for (name in required_params)
  if (is.null(params[[name]]) || !nzchar(params[[name]]))
    stop("Missing parameter: ", name)

read_metrics <- function(path, expected_model) {
  x <- read.delim(normalizePath(path, mustWork=TRUE), sep="\t",
                  stringsAsFactors=FALSE, check.names=FALSE)
  if (nrow(x) != 63) stop("Expected 63 rows in ", path, "; found ", nrow(x))
  if (!all(x$model == expected_model)) stop("Model mismatch in ", path)
  if (!all(x$negative_kind == params$negative_kind))
    stop("Background-type mismatch in ", path)
  x
}

x <- bind_rows(
  read_metrics(params$alphagenome_metrics_path, "alphagenome"),
  read_metrics(params$lsgkm_metrics_path, "lsgkm")
) |>
  mutate(
    Model=factor(recode(model, alphagenome="AlphaGenome", lsgkm="LS-GKM"),
                 levels=c("AlphaGenome", "LS-GKM")),
    Split=factor(recode(split, train_100="Full training pool",
                        validation="Validation", test="Test"),
                 levels=c("Full training pool", "Validation", "Test")),
    ranking_error=1-auroc
  ) |>
  arrange(Model, Split, checkpoint_index)

if (nrow(x) != 126) stop("Expected 126 combined metric rows; found ", nrow(x))
if (n_distinct(x$dataset) != 1) stop("Dataset mismatch between model inputs")

metric_limits <- function(v) {
  span <- diff(range(v, na.rm=TRUE)); pad <- max(span*.08, .002)
  range(v, na.rm=TRUE) + c(-pad, pad)
}

learning_plot <- function(metric, title, label) {
  ggplot(x, aes(checkpoint_index, .data[[metric]], color=Model, group=Model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth=.85) + geom_point(size=1.8) +
    facet_grid(Split ~ Model, scales="free_x") +
    scale_color_manual(values=model_colors) +
    chromosome_x_scale(x) + chromosome_x_theme() +
    coord_cartesian(ylim=metric_limits(x[[metric]])) +
    labs(title=title, x="Training endpoint chromosome", y=label, color="Model") +
    guides(color="none")
}
```

# Scope and interpretation

This report compares native `r params$analysis_name` performance for AlphaGenome
and LS-GKM using `r params$negative_kind` negative backgrounds.
`r params$positive_class` sequences have label 1 and matched negative-background
sequences have label 0. Chr1 is validation, chr2 is held-out test, and training
checkpoints cumulatively add chr3 through chrX.

Each panel contains one task trajectory. Columns place the two model families
side by side, while rows show the full training pool, validation, and test on
common metric-axis ranges.

# AUROC learning curves

```{r auroc}
learning_plot("auroc", paste(params$analysis_name, "AUROC"), "AUROC")
```

# Average-precision learning curves

```{r auprc}
learning_plot("auprc", paste(params$analysis_name, "average precision"),
              "Average Precision")
```

# AUROC ranking-error curves

```{r ranking}
learning_plot("ranking_error", paste(params$analysis_name, "AUROC ranking error"),
              "1 - AUROC")
```

# Chromosome composition

```{r chromosome-composition, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
composition <- chromosome_composition(x |>
  transmute(Group=params$analysis_name, Split, checkpoint_index,
            endpoint_chromosome, n_training_total, n_evaluation_total))
chromosome_composition_plot(composition)
```

# Full-training comparison

```{r full}
x |> filter(checkpoint_index == max(checkpoint_index)) |>
  select(Model, Split, n_training_total, n_evaluation_total, auroc, auprc) |>
  rename(`Training observations`=n_training_total,
         `Evaluation observations`=n_evaluation_total,
         AUROC=auroc, `Average Precision`=auprc) |>
  arrange(Model, Split) |>
  gt(groupname_col="Model") |>
  tab_header(title="Final chr3-through-chrX models") |>
  fmt_integer(columns=c(`Training observations`, `Evaluation observations`)) |>
  fmt_number(columns=c(AUROC, `Average Precision`), decimals=3)
```

# Reproducibility notes

- Both methods use the same chromosome-defined task datasets.
- Every checkpoint is independently trained.
- Metric y-axis ranges are shared across methods and evaluation splits.
- Test data are used only for final evaluation.
- AlphaGenome uses logits from validation-selected frozen-encoder heads; LS-GKM uses continuous gkm-SVM decision scores.

Rendered at `r format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z")`.
